$comment: The JSON API's numbers and mappings (agentcake/api/). The words of its answers are in api.en.json, the dashboard's coverage note in coverage.en.json, the home page's example in example.json. Times in ms unless the key says otherwise.
$ranges: The date ranges of the dashboard and the session list (agentcake/api/periods.py), PostHog's, in menu order. range_hours: from the start of the hour that many hours ago, in AgentCake's timezone (PostHog's -24h): the Trends chart's first hour is a whole one. range_days: from midnight that many days ago (PostHog's -7d and -30d), so today is one more of their days. The Agent block compares each with its previous period, as PostHog's web analytics does: as long as the range runs to the end of its current hour or day, right before it.
$verdicts: The verdict (judging.en.json 'verdicts') of each class verdict.py gives and of cake 0.3.4's verdict column (human, agent, unsure): mixed is an Agent session; Not sure and Too little data are Human, marked: evidence 'thin' (a session cake can't tell is counted as human, and marked; the reasons say why), as is a session not judged yet. agent_turns splits an Agent session: Agent only, or Human + agent (a human and an agent took turns). certainty: how sure an agent's or a bot's name is, by attribute.py's certainty (verified names are certain). layer_states: a layer's state as the reasons panel shows it (the behavior layer's mixed: Human + agent).

reasons.$comment: Where a verdict's reason shows in the four layers of 'Why this classification', and the kind of evidence the page draws its icon for. A reason shows in the layer its evidence belongs to: the layer layer_by_id names for its id first (a name read off a product's or a tool's trace in the page is the environment's finding, as a verdict judged before it moved there kept it under name), else its own, and comes after the layer's own reasons (a name after the trace it was read from); a reason of a layer the page does not have (weak signals, crawler-like patterns) goes to other_layers; exclusion reasons only come with prefetches, which are no visit. kind: by_id first, then an environment rule's own kind (env_rule_kinds), then the half it was read from (by_source), then the layer's default.
reasons.$turns: A session whose timeline has hand-offs (a Human + agent session) shows its behavior layer as Human + agent, whatever the model said of the session as a whole, and words the model's own line as these say (the timeline's turns are the behavior layer's finding).
reasons.$bot: A Bot session whose environment layer found an agent's traces says why it is still a Bot (api.en.json 'layer_notes', bot_environment, in the layer bot_note_layer names); a layer less than half sure of its own conclusion reads Unknown and says why first (layer_notes both_ways).
reasons.$agree: A layer lists only the reasons that fit the conclusion it shows (a reason for one side beside that side's conclusion; a layer that can't tell lists both); only_when names the conclusions a reason belongs to.

summary.$comment: How the session page sums up a verdict (agentcake/api/session.py): who acted when, from the timeline's runs; for a session without runs to tell (a bot, a Human one on thin evidence), the first reason in the verdict's tone, else the first of fallback_layer; a session without reasons gets the rule of its class (judging.en.json; 'classes', by its agent_turns for an Agent session, 'thin' for a Human one on thin evidence, else its verdict, for a verdict from before 0.4.0). Then the layers whose conclusion is the verdict's ('supports': the layer states that agree with it), each with its percent when the layer shows one.

settings.$comment: The settings page. refresh_ms: how often the open page asks again where visits come from, so that the first visit shows as connected within 10 s. server_half_tokens: how many of the latest server-half tokens tell which request headers never reached the site's server (none of them had it: something in front of the server removes it). server_half_headers: those headers, by their role in edge.json; a browser sends them on every page request over HTTPS, which Sec-Fetch-User is not (only after a click).
